title: Quantization perf/quality tradeoffs: INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ kernels (v2)
content:
Summary:

This note captures the latest set of micro- and macro-benchmarks for quantized inference kernels across INT8 (GPTQ), INT8 (AWQ), and FP8 formats. Goal is to document measured latency/throughput, memory usage, and end-to-end quality regressions for representative open models and kernels we run in the serving runtime. This is an iteration (v2) of previous bench runs — added consistent P99 reporting, more seeds for QA, and kernel-level profiling traces.

Goals:
- Produce apples-to-apples comparison of INT8(GPTQ), INT8(AWQ), FP8, and FP16 baseline for throughput/latency and quality.
- Surface per-kernel hotspots (GEMM, fused attention, KV cache ops) and how quantization affects them.
- Provide recommendations for default quantization profiles & fallback policies in the runtime.

Testbed / environment:
- Hardware: NVIDIA A10G (driver 535.86), 40GB VRAM, single-GPU for microbenchmarks; Dedicated pool nodes (4x A10G) for throughput tests.
- Software: serving-runtime@main (commit 0a9f3b), CUDA 12.1, cuBLAS/cuDNN as system libs. Custom fused kernels compiled with nvcc 12.2.
- Models: Llama-2-13b-chat (community variant), Mistral-7B, and a 2B instruction-tuned checkpoint.
- Workloads: 1) zero-shot generation (instruction prompt, average gen length = 128 tokens), 2) chat-like 4-turn convo (context 2k tokens), 3) embedding generation (not quantified in this doc).

Methodology:
- Baselines: FP16 (serving default) measured first; quantized versions loaded with identical tokenizer & sampling params to isolate model arithmetic changes.
- Repeats: each measurement is median of 5 runs (each run 200 requests for latency tests). Report P50 and P99 latencies and steady-state tokens/sec throughput.
- Quality metrics: perplexity on held-out validation shards, and an instruction-following automated metric (pairwise BLEU/ROUGE-L vs reference completions). Also ran a small human eval (n=120 prompts) for edge-case hallucination checks — summarized below.
- Profiling: nvprof / Nsight traces for hot-kernel breakdown; lightweight CPU flame traces to capture host-side overhead (serialization, IO).

Kernels instrumented:
- matmul_gemm_fused (dense GEMM path)
- attention_fused (softmax + scale + matmul + fused mask)
- kv_cache_write/read
- tokenizer + sampling host loop (CPU-bound)
- custom quant_dequant kernels for GPTQ/AWQ paths

Key results (representative numbers):

Llama-2-13B (baseline FP16):
- P50 latency (token): 16.8 ms
- P99 latency (token): 48.2 ms
- Throughput (steady tokens/sec): 95 tok/s
- VRAM footprint (load+cache): 16.8 GB
- Perplexity (val shard): 8.30
- Human eval score (instruction-following normalized): 0.86

INT8 (GPTQ) - Llama-2-13B:
- P50 latency: 13.4 ms (20% improvement vs FP16)
- P99 latency: 41.0 ms (15% improvement)
- Throughput: 122 tok/s (+28%)
- VRAM: 9.6 GB (drop ~43%)
- Perplexity: 8.95 (+7.8% regression)
- Human eval: 0.79 (notable drop on commonsense QA prompts)
- Notes: matmul_gemm_fused dominates time fraction (~62%). Dequant path and per-block reorder in GPTQ contribute ~6% host overhead.

INT8 (AWQ) - Llama-2-13B:
- P50 latency: 13.7 ms
- P99 latency: 42.1 ms
- Throughput: 118 tok/s (+24%)
- VRAM: 10.0 GB
- Perplexity: 8.52 (+2.7% regression)
- Human eval: 0.83 (minor degradation, better than GPTQ on some reasoning prompts)
- Notes: AWQ quant approach kept per-block scale factors and produced higher numeric fidelity; kernel incorporation required an extra fused dequant strategy but the host overhead was similar to GPTQ (~5%).

FP8 (experimental kernels) - Llama-2-13B:
- P50 latency: 15.0 ms (10% improvement)
- P99 latency: 45.0 ms
- Throughput: 104 tok/s (+9%)
- VRAM: 12.2 GB
- Perplexity: 8.40 (+1.2% regression)
- Human eval: 0.85 (near parity with FP16)
- Notes: FP8 requires FP8-capable GEMM kernels and careful accumulation to avoid overflow; with our current kernel implementation we see lower speedups than INT8 but better quality retention.

Mistral-7B (summary):
- FP16 baseline throughput: 140 tok/s
- INT8(GPTQ): 185 tok/s (+32%), perplexity +9% (noticeable in long-context tasks)
- INT8(AWQ): 178 tok/s (+27%), perplexity +3%
- FP8: 152 tok/s (+8%), perplexity +0.8%

Per-kernel breakdown (Llama-2-13B, INT8 GPTQ example):
- matmul_gemm_fused: 62% of GPU time (hotspot)
- attention_fused: 18%
- kv_cache io: 8%
- quant/dequant overhead: 6% (host-GPU roundtrips cause small stalls)
- sampling & tokenizer (CPU): 6% (insensitive to quant choice)

Observations and interpretation:
- INT8 offers the largest win in VRAM and throughput. However, GPTQ-produced weight permutations/compactions result in measurable quality degradation for some models; AWQ consistently narrows that gap while still providing a large efficiency benefit.
- FP8, while promising for quality parity, currently gives smaller speedups because our FP8 GEMM kernels are not as optimized as cuBLAS/FP16 paths. With more kernel tuning (tiling, vectorization) FP8 could be competitive.
- P99 improvements are smaller than median improvements — indicates tail latency drivers include KV cache writes and host-side quant/dequant stalling. We should prioritize async memory transfers and overlapping quant transforms.
- Host-side overhead for quant-specific transforms is non-trivial. For high-concurrency environments, we should batch quantization pre-processing and move dequant to fused kernels where possible.

Recommendations for runtime defaults:
- Default profile: enable AWQ for public/recommended open models (13B+), enable GPTQ as a more aggressive footprint option but mark as "quality-risk" in the console.
- FP8: add as opt-in experimental profile; only enable for customers who request highest quality with some kernel flags.
- Kernel work: prioritize optimizing INT8 GEMM and FP8 GEMM; implement fused quant/dequant within attention kernel to reduce host-GPU synchronization.
- Fallbacks: auto-fallback to FP16 if per-route QA checks detect >5% automated metric regression during canary rollout.

Open questions / next steps:
- Run the same benchmark suite across DGX A100/RTX 6000 to capture cross-hardware kernel performance differences.
- Increase human-eval pool (n>=500) focusing on reasoning and factuality to quantify subtle quality regressions.
- Evaluate mixed-precision per-layer policies (e.g., keep norm & first/last layers in FP16).
- Add microbench for multi-GPU sharded setups to capture all-reduce overheads with quantized tensors.

Appendix (commands / notes):
- Benchmark driver: tools/bench/quant_bench.py --model llama-2-13b --profile awq --batch 1 --gen-len 128 --repeat 5
- Profiling: nv-nsight-cu-cli --sample 100 --output out.nsys "python tools/bench/quant_bench.py ..."
- Kernel build flags: NVCC_FLAGS="-O3 -arch=sm_86 -lineinfo" make -C kernels fp8_gemm

Notes to reviewers:
- Numbers are preliminary but consistent across repeated runs on our testbed. Sharing to capture feedback on fallback thresholds and rollout policy language for product/console teams.
- Attached traces and raw CSVs are on the PR (linked above) — will add more comparisons vs other open checkpoints in next iteration.
